Fit a Gaussian mixture to a characteristic function

Source: R/from_cf.R
from_cf.Rd

Fits a Gaussian mixture to a distribution that is known through its characteristic function \(\varphi(t) = E \exp(i t^\top X)\). No density and no sample of the distribution are needed. The result is an ordinary fitted mixture, so rgmm(), dgmm(), gmm_affine(), gmm_convolve() and the other mixture operations apply to it.

Usage

from_cf(
  cf,
  n_dim,
  N,
  n_freq = 8192L,
  bandwidths = c(0.3, 0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5),
  n_start = 1L,
  max_iter = 300L,
  init = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

cf

A function that takes an n by n_dim matrix of frequencies, one per row, and returns the characteristic function at each row as a complex vector of length n. A real vector is accepted for a symmetric target.

n_dim

Dimension of the target.

N

Number of mixture components.

n_freq

Number of frequencies in the fit, at least 64 times length(bandwidths). Default 8192L.

bandwidths

Increasing positive numbers, the typical length of a frequency vector in units of the target's half-height frequency (each coordinate has standard deviation bandwidth / sqrt(n_dim) of that). The grown start and init use all bandwidths together. Random starts are fitted from the lowest bandwidth upwards. Extend the range upwards for a target with fine structure and downwards for a heavy-tailed target.

n_start

Number of starts. The first start is init if given, otherwise the grown start described above; the others are random. The fit with the lowest loss is returned. Default 1L. With ten or more components in five or more dimensions a single start can stop at a poor fit, so four starts are a safer choice. For ten components in ten dimensions the grown start stopped at a poor fit and a random start recovered the target.

max_iter

Maximum number of L-BFGS iterations per frequency stage. A Levenberg-Marquardt step with at most 200 iterations follows when the fit has at most 700 parameters. Default 300L.

init

Optional gmm with N components to start the first fit from, in place of the grown start. Default NULL.

seed

Optional integer seed. When supplied, the random number generator state is restored on exit.

Value

A gmm_fit with regime set to NA. Its diagnostics hold loss (the final loss), loss_by_start, loss_path (the loss as the grown start went from 1 to N components, or NULL when init is given), heldout_rms and heldout_max, relocations (the number of moves kept), tail_index (one value for each coordinate), cf_mean and cf_cov (the target's mean and covariance read from cf, or NULL when the target has no finite, positive definite covariance), n_freq and bandwidths. converged is FALSE when the final optimisation of the returned fit stopped at its iteration limit.

Details

The fit minimises the mean of \(|\varphi(t_j) - \varphi_g(t_j)|^2\) over a fixed sample of frequencies \(t_j\), where \(\varphi_g\) is the characteristic function of the mixture (gmm_cf()). The frequencies are Gaussian with several bandwidths, scaled to the target so that bandwidths = 1 is the frequency at which \(|\varphi|\) has fallen to about one half. The same criterion is used by Brück (2025) to train a neural sampler.

The starting mixture is built one component at a time. Each new component is placed at the mean where the fit falls furthest short of the target, after both are smoothed by a Gaussian. That mean is computed from the characteristic-function residual, so no density of the target is needed. All components are refitted after each addition. The fit then tries moving each of the two least useful components to a better mean, keeping a move if it cuts the loss by at least 10%, up to N moves.

Checking a fit

The returned object reports the root mean square and the maximum of \(|\varphi - \varphi_g|\) on n_freq fresh frequencies that the fit did not use (heldout_rms and heldout_max in diagnostics). gmm_cf_distance() gives a lower and an upper bound for the Kolmogorov distance between the target and the fit along any direction.

Heavy tails

A Gaussian mixture has finite moments of every order, so it cannot reproduce infinite-variance tails and fits the centre only. The tail index is read from \(-\log|\varphi|\) near zero. It is 2 when the variance is finite and equals the stability index for a stable law. When it is below 1.9 a warning of class proxymix_cf_heavy_tail is raised.

Scope

The target needs a characteristic function that decays, which excludes lattice distributions and distributions with a point mass.

References

Brück, F. (2025). Generative neural networks for characteristic functions. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 34(4), 1456–1465. doi:10.1080/10618600.2025.2455135

See also

gmm_cf(), gmm_cf_distance().

Other fitting: fit_em_samples(), fit_kld_em(), fit_moment_match(), fit_mppca_samples(), from_cf_elliptical(), from_cf_sources(), from_kde(), from_objective(), select_N()

Examples

## The sum of a Gamma(3) variable and independent N(0, 0.25) noise.
cf <- function(t) (1 - 1i * t[, 1])^(-3) * exp(-0.125 * t[, 1]^2)
fit <- from_cf(cf, n_dim = 1L, N = 3L, n_freq = 1024L, seed = 1L)
fit@diagnostics$heldout_rms
#> [1] 0.004769877
gmm_cf_distance(fit, cf)$distance
#> [1] 0.003982315
